draft.title: Injunctions
card: An injunction is a court order that tells a person to act in a certain way, or to stop. It is a remedy that is not paid in money.
an order to stop doing something, or not to start, such as stopping a business from making loud noise at night.
an order to do something, such as removing a fence built on a neighbour's land.
A person who ignores an injunction can be punished by the court for contempt of court. Injunctions are often used when money would not fix the problem.
draft.remember: A restrictive injunction orders a person to stop. A mandatory one orders them to act.

a.q: A court orders a factory in Dandenong to stop dumping waste into a creek. What kind of order is this?
a.why: The order tells the factory to stop doing something, so it is a restrictive injunction. A mandatory injunction would order the factory to do something, such as clean up the creek.
a.clue: Is the order telling the factory to stop or to act?

b.q: Leila builds a shed that blocks her neighbour's driveway in Bendigo. The court orders her to knock it down. What kind of order is this?
b.why: Knocking the shed down is something Leila must do, so the order is a mandatory injunction. A restrictive injunction would only stop her from doing something, such as stopping her building more.
b.clue: Ask whether Leila must take an action.
